concepts.name: Mutex vs blocking locks in coroutines
Room foreign keys: child-column indices and deferred checks

questions.prompt: A token cache must let only one coroutine at a time run `refreshIfExpired()`, which calls a suspend network function. Why do the coroutines docs point you to `Mutex.withLock { }` rather than a blocking lock?

choices.text: Waiting coroutines suspend on `lock()`, so no thread is blocked meanwhile
`Mutex` is reentrant, so a nested `withLock` in one coroutine can't deadlock
`Mutex` marks the guarded fields `@Volatile`, which makes their updates atomic
`Mutex` moves the critical section onto its own single dedicated thread

questions.explanation: `Mutex.lock()` is a suspending function: a coroutine waiting for the lock suspends and frees its thread, while a blocking lock makes every waiter hold its thread. `Mutex` is not reentrant (locking it again from the holder suspends forever), it doesn't change how fields behave (and `@Volatile` wouldn't make an update atomic anyway), and it doesn't own a thread: running everything on one thread is a different technique, thread confinement.

sources.title: Shared mutable state and concurrency
sources.claim: `Mutex.lock()` is a suspending function and does not block a thread; `withLock` wraps lock/try/finally unlock; volatile does not make larger actions atomic; thread confinement is a separate technique using a single-threaded context.

sources.title: Mutex
sources.claim: Mutex is non-reentrant: invoking `lock` even from the coroutine that currently holds the lock still suspends the invoker; `lock` suspends the caller until the lock is acquired.

questions.prompt: A Room `Comment` entity declares `ForeignKey(entity = Post::class, parentColumns = ["id"], childColumns = ["postId"], onDelete = ForeignKey.CASCADE)` but no index on `postId`. What does Room do?

choices.text: It fails to compile, because every foreign key needs an index on its child
It compiles with a warning: each change to a post may scan every comment
It quietly adds the missing index on `postId` when it creates the table
Nothing: a child index only matters for queries that filter on `postId`

questions.explanation: Room requires a unique index (or the primary key) on the parent columns and fails the build without one, but for the child side it only prints `MISSING_INDEX_ON_FOREIGN_KEY_CHILD`. The warning matters: without an index on `postId`, deleting or updating a post makes SQLite scan the whole comment table to find the rows that reference it. Room doesn't add the index for you; declare `indices = [Index("postId")]`.

sources.title: ForeignKey
sources.claim: Room requires a unique index or primary key on the parent columns (compile-time error otherwise), recommends an index on the child columns to avoid full table scans when the parent changes and prints MISSING_INDEX_ON_FOREIGN_KEY_CHILD if it is missing; constraints are immediate by default but can be deferred to the end of the transaction with `deferred = true`, which helps bulk inserts.

sources.title: SQLite Foreign Key Support
sources.claim: Without an index on the child key, deleting a parent row requires a linear scan of the whole child table, so an index should be created on the child key columns of each foreign key; ON DELETE CASCADE deletes the child rows of a deleted parent.

questions.prompt: A location SDK offers `client.requestLocation(callback): Request`, with `onResult(location)`, `onError(e)` and `request.cancel()`. Wrap it as `suspend fun currentLocation(): Location` so that a cancelled caller doesn't leave the request running. Which builder do you use, and how do you handle each outcome?

model_answer.summary: Use `suspendCancellableCoroutine`: resume with the location, resume with the exception on error, and cancel the SDK request in `invokeOnCancellation`, so cancelling the caller cancels the work.
key_points: Use `suspendCancellableCoroutine` (not `suspendCoroutine`): its `CancellableContinuation` makes the caller throw `CancellationException` when its Job is cancelled while suspended
Register `invokeOnCancellation { request.cancel() }` so the SDK request (or callback registration) is cleaned up when the caller is cancelled
Prompt cancellation: once the caller's Job is cancelled it won't resume successfully, even if the callback already called `resume`, so a late result is dropped

questions.explanation: `suspendCancellableCoroutine` is the bridge from a one-shot callback to a suspend function that respects structured concurrency. Resuming with the result or the error turns the callback into a return value or an exception, and `invokeOnCancellation` is where you undo the registration, so leaving the screen stops the SDK work. Retrofit's own `Call.await()` is built this way.

sources.title: suspendCancellableCoroutine
sources.claim: suspendCancellableCoroutine gives a CancellableContinuation and throws CancellationException if the Job is cancelled while suspended; `invokeOnCancellation` unregisters callbacks; with the prompt cancellation guarantee the caller does not resume successfully if its Job was cancelled, even if `resume` was already invoked.

sources.title: retrofit2/KotlinExtensions.kt (Retrofit source)
sources.claim: `Call.await()` resumes with the body for a successful response, resumes with `HttpException(response)` for an unsuccessful one, and registers `invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }` so cancelling the coroutine cancels the Call; `awaitResponse()` resumes with the Response whatever its status.

choices.text: `log()` joins the lock already held, so it runs at once without waiting
`log()` blocks the thread until `save()` releases the lock it is holding
The coroutine suspends forever in `log()`, as `Mutex` isn't reentrant
Nothing odd: `withLock` lets the coroutine that holds a lock lock it again

questions.explanation: `Mutex` is non-reentrant: calling `lock` from the coroutine that already holds it still suspends the caller, and the holder can't release it while it waits, so `save()` never finishes. It suspends rather than blocking a thread. Take the lock once at the outer level and call an unlocked helper inside.

questions.prompt: A sync job inserts comments before their posts inside one Room transaction, and the inserts fail on the foreign key constraint. Which `ForeignKey` option fits this?

choices.text: `deferred = true`, so the constraint is checked when the transaction ends
`onDelete = ForeignKey.CASCADE`, so the missing parent rows are created
`onUpdate = ForeignKey.NO_ACTION`, so that inserts skip the parent check
`Index("postId", unique = true)`, so a child can exist without its parent

questions.explanation: Foreign key constraints are checked immediately by default. Setting `deferred = true` delays the check until the transaction completes, which the Room docs suggest for bulk inserts, so the comments are valid once their posts are inserted in the same transaction. `CASCADE` and `NO_ACTION` only say what happens when a parent is deleted or updated, and an index doesn't relax the constraint.

questions.prompt: Inside `suspendCancellableCoroutine`, the SDK callback calls `cont.resume(value)`, but the caller's Job is cancelled before the caller has resumed running. What does the caller get?

choices.text: `value`, because `resume` was called before the Job was cancelled
Nothing yet: it stays suspended until the callback fires once more
An `IllegalStateException`, for resuming a cancelled continuation
A `CancellationException`: the resumed value is never delivered

questions.explanation: `suspendCancellableCoroutine` has a prompt cancellation guarantee: if the Job was cancelled while the function was suspended, it doesn't resume successfully even if `resume` was already called. The caller throws `CancellationException` and the value is dropped, so code after the call never sees a result for a cancelled operation.

sources.title: suspendCancellableCoroutine
sources.claim: suspendCancellableCoroutine gives a CancellableContinuation and throws CancellationException if the Job is cancelled while suspended; `invokeOnCancellation` unregisters callbacks; with the prompt cancellation guarantee the caller does not resume successfully if its Job was cancelled, even if `resume` was already invoked.

questions.prompt: You wrap a location SDK (`requestLocation(callback): Request`, with `onResult`, `onError` and `request.cancel()`) as `suspend fun currentLocation(): Location`. A cancelled caller must not leave the request running. Select all that apply.

choices.text: Build it with `suspendCancellableCoroutine`, not plain `suspendCoroutine`
A late `resume(location)` still hands the value to a caller already cancelled
Call `resumeWithException(e)` from `onError` so the caller gets the error
`invokeOnCancellation` runs each time the SDK calls `onResult` successfully
Register `invokeOnCancellation { request.cancel() }` to stop the request

questions.explanation: `suspendCancellableCoroutine` gives a `CancellableContinuation`, so the caller throws `CancellationException` if its Job is cancelled while suspended. Resume with the location from `onResult` and with the exception from `onError`. `invokeOnCancellation` installs a handler that runs when the suspended coroutine is cancelled (not on success), which is where you cancel the SDK request. Its prompt cancellation guarantee means a cancelled caller does not resume successfully, even if `resume` was already called, so a late location is dropped.

sources.title: suspendCancellableCoroutine
sources.claim: `suspendCancellableCoroutine` gives a `CancellableContinuation` that can be resumed with a value or an exception and throws `CancellationException` if the Job is cancelled while suspended; `invokeOnCancellation` installs a handler called when the suspended coroutine is cancelled; with the prompt cancellation guarantee the coroutine does not resume successfully if its Job was cancelled, even if `resume` was already invoked.
